name: Egypt
overview: Scripture presents Egypt as a significant land marked by both blessing and trial, serving as a place of refuge during famine, as seen when Abram sojourned there (Genesis 12:10, 13:1). It is described as a fertile and well-watered land, comparable to the garden of the LORD (Genesis 13:10). Egypt also represents a place of future affliction for Abraham’s descendants, who would be strangers and servants there for four hundred years before God’s judgment and their eventual deliverance with great substance (Genesis 15:13-14). Furthermore, God’s covenant with Abraham extends to the land from the river of Egypt to the Euphrates, highlighting Egypt’s geographical and theological significance (Genesis 15:18).
